about: Hand-written rotation guides for the paladin's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: Retribution in a raid twists seals: you swap between **Seal of Righteousness** and **Seal of Command** around every swing so each hit carries both, judge **Seal of Righteousness** on cooldown, and give the remaining global cooldowns to **Consecration**, **Holy Strike** and, under 20% health, **Hammer of Wrath**.
why: Only one seal can be active, so keeping up two seals means a twist: with **Twist of Light**, replacing a seal leaves an Echo of it that your next melee swing applies. The full rotation casts **Seal of Righteousness** in the last 0.4 seconds before each swing and **Seal of Command** after the swing, in any global cooldown that **Hammer of Wrath**, **Consecration** and **Holy Strike** do not need: about 14 and 12 times a minute. Opening with **Seal of Command** means your very first swing already carries both.

Press **Judgement** every time it is ready while **Seal of Righteousness** is up, whether or not the short list shows it. It is off the global cooldown, comes back every 8 seconds with **Improved Judgement**, no longer uses up your seal in Forever, and **Sanctified Judgement** returns 60% of the seal's mana cost; in the simulator the judgement of **Seal of Righteousness** is about an eighth of your damage. If it comes off cooldown while **Seal of Command** is up, judge anyway.

**Hammer of Wrath** goes first once the boss is below 20% health: with 2 points in **Instrument of Law** it is instant, it comes back every 6 seconds, and at about 500 Holy damage plus a share of your spell damage it is your biggest single hit.

**Consecration** comes before **Holy Strike** while you have at least a quarter of your mana: on a single boss it deals 312 Holy damage over 8 seconds plus a share of your spell damage, about a sixth of your damage in the simulator, and **Holy Conduit** makes it 40% cheaper.

**Holy Strike** sits last but is not a real filler: it has a 10-second cooldown, so press it whenever it is ready (20 mana, and **Sacred Arbiter** adds 20% to it). The global cooldowns between your other buttons go to the seal swaps.

**Seal of Command** is always rank 4: every rank adds the same 70% of weapon damage, rank 4 costs 30 mana less, and the simulator measured it 0.3% better than rank 5. When mana runs low the full rotation steps down: **Seal of Righteousness** rank 7 below half mana, **Seal of Command** rank 2 below 30%, a rank 1 **Consecration** below a quarter, and no seal swaps at all below 15%.
caveats: The twist rests on the simulator's reading of **Twist of Light**: every Echo you have up fires on the next swing, so a swing after both swaps applies **Seal of Righteousness** twice (the seal and its Echo) and **Seal of Command**'s chance once. If the game allows only one Echo per swing, one swap per swing, alternating the two seals, does the same work with half the global cooldowns: check it at launch.

All those swaps cost mana, even 20% cheaper with **Twist of Light**. The full-raid numbers assume the raid's **Blessing of Wisdom**, Mana Spring and other paladins' judgements of **Seal of Wisdom** and **Seal of the Crusader** on the boss; with only your own buffs the simulator keeps **Seal of Righteousness** up and twists on every swing only while your mana is above about two thirds.

Forever weakens ranks far below your level, and the simulator applies an assumed formula (TBC's) since 2026-10-09. **Seal of Command** rank 4 and **Seal of Righteousness** rank 7 are close enough to 60 to lose nothing, but rank 1 **Consecration** keeps only a bit over half of its spell damage bonus, so it is a low-mana stopgap only; the game may also lower a low rank's chance to trigger effects, which no simulator models.
Several targets: only **Consecration** spreads (its bonus damage hits the first four enemies in it); your seals, judgements and **Holy Strike** stay on one target.
diverge: If you cannot time your swings (no swing timer, high latency), skip the swaps: keep **Seal of Righteousness** up, judge it on cooldown and press **Consecration** and **Holy Strike**. How much that costs on the current beta build was not measured.

Against an Undead or Demon boss, add **Exorcism** on cooldown (15 seconds, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**): it hits harder than **Holy Strike**. The simulator's target is an Elemental, so where it fits best was not measured.
When you have to leave melee range, keep pressing **Judgement** (10 yards) and, under 20%, **Hammer of Wrath** (30 yards); your seals only work on swings.

leveling.plan: Retribution levels with one seal: **Seal of Command** before each pull, **Judgement** and **Holy Strike** on cooldown, and your mana kept for judgements and heals instead of **Consecration**.
why: **Seal of Command** goes up before each pull (from level 20; **Seal of Righteousness** before that) and lasts 30 seconds, longer than most fights. It adds a Holy hit of 70% of your weapon damage about 7 times a minute, so a slow two-hander suits it; this build has no **Twist of Light**, so there is no seal swapping while leveling.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready: **Judgement** is off the global cooldown and comes back every 8 seconds with **Improved Judgement**, and **Sanctified Judgement** (levels 21 to 23) returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time. The open search found **Sanctified Judgement** the most valuable talent of this build at 60, for the drinking it saves.
**Consecration** is for two or more mobs. Against a single mob the fight lab's tuned rotation never casts it and kills about 5% faster that way: its mana costs more drinking than its damage saves.

**Hammer of Justice** doubles **Seal of Command**'s judgement: against a stunned mob it hits for 339 to 373 instead of 169 to 187 at rank 5. When both are ready and the mob has more than 30% health left, stun first, then judge; otherwise keep the stun for a caster or for when you are hurt.
**Hammer of Wrath** finishes mobs below 20% health from level 44, and it is instant once you have 2 points in **Instrument of Law** (levels 35 and 36).

Below about a third of your health, while the mob still has a quarter of its own: **Divine Protection** (8 seconds immune, but you cannot attack) with **Holy Light** inside it, or **Hammer of Justice** and heal during the stun; **Flash of Light** below a quarter, **Lay on Hands** below 15%. Between fights heal back to 80%; the tuned rotation drinks only below 15% of your mana.
caveats: Several mobs: **Consecration** hits all of them and its bonus damage goes to the first four in it, so it earns its mana there. The fight lab's three-mob runs still played without it, so the gain is unmeasured.

Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** (instant, 30 yards, 15-second cooldown, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**) hits them hard, and **Holy Wrath** handles packs. The fight lab has no Undead or Demon mobs, so neither was measured.
diverge: A mob that stands back and casts: **Hammer of Justice** (10 yards) stops the cast; the fight lab uses it that way.
A mob that runs at low health: **Hammer of Wrath** (30 yards) finishes it, or **Hammer of Justice** holds it.

raid.plan: Most of your threat is Holy damage, and **Righteous Fury** makes it 60% more threat. Keep **Holy Shield** up, judge **Seal of Righteousness** on cooldown and press **Consecration** and **Holy Strike** whenever they are ready; **Templar's Bulwark** and **Lay on Hands** are your emergency buttons.
why: Before the pull: **Righteous Fury** (it lasts 30 minutes, and **Improved Righteous Fury** and **Iron Creed** only work while it is up), then **Seal of Righteousness** and **Holy Shield** in the last seconds, so the first hits already meet both.

**Holy Shield** lasts 10 seconds and comes back every 10, so keep it up all fight: 30% more block for 4 blocks, and every block deals Holy damage with 20% extra threat and can trigger **Redoubt** and **Shield Specialization**'s mana. The simulator measured 1.3% more tank value with it at the top of the list.

Press **Judgement** on cooldown, whether or not the short list shows it: it is off the global cooldown, judges **Seal of Righteousness** for about a tenth of your threat, and no longer uses up the seal in Forever. Judging every time it is ready, instead of only before the seal runs out, measured 4.3% more tank value; **Swift Judgement** goes right after a **Judgement**, because it finishes the cooldown and makes the next one free.

**Consecration** and **Holy Strike** fill the rest: **Consecration** threatens everything standing in it, and **Holy Strike** with **Iron Creed** makes 25% more threat and cuts your damage taken by 10% for 6 seconds. Refresh **Seal of Righteousness** when it has about a second left.

**Templar's Bulwark** sits at the top because the simulator's 3-minute fight fits one use: it absorbs damage equal to your maximum health for 8 seconds, off the global cooldown, and using it at the pull measured 1.4% more tank value. It applies Forbearance for a minute, which locks you out of **Divine Protection**, **Divine Shield** and **Blessing of Protection**.

**Lay on Hands** below 10% health measured 8% more tank value, but nobody heals you in the simulator's fights. In a raid it is the last resort: it heals you for your maximum health and drains all your mana.
caveats: The simulator tanks with **Seal of Righteousness**. **Seal of Fury** (35 Holy damage a swing, plus an absorb of half of it while you hold a shield) is not part of its tuned rotation, so whether it is better for you was not measured.

Mana: you run dry for a few seconds of each 3-minute fight in the simulator. **Consecration** is the expensive button (565 mana before **Holy Conduit**); blocks give mana back through **Shield Specialization** and judgements through **Sanctified Judgement**.
The simulator measures one boss. **Consecration** and **Holy Shield** work on everything that hits you; **Holy Strike** and **Judgement** only on your target.
diverge: To taunt (a tank swap, a loose add), put up **Seal of Fury** and judge: its judgement taunts for 4 seconds. Use **Swift Judgement** if **Judgement** is on cooldown, then go back to **Seal of Righteousness**.
Hold **Templar's Bulwark** for a known damage spike or a healer death when the fight has one: the simulator spends it at the pull only because its fight fits a single use.

Undead or Demon packs: **Holy Wrath** (a 2-second cast) hits and stuns every Undead and Demon within 20 yards, and **Exorcism** hits one hard. Neither was measured: the simulator's boss is an Elemental.

leveling.plan: Protection levels behind a shield: **Seal of Fury** turns half of its Holy damage into an absorb, blocks and judgements pay your mana back, and **Judgement**, **Holy Strike** and **Consecration** do the damage, so you rarely stop to eat.
why: **Seal of Fury** before each pull: at rank 7 it adds 35 Holy damage to every swing, and with a shield each swing also gives you an absorb of half that damage; **Improved Seal of Fury** returns 60 mana each time such a shield is used up.
Keep **Righteous Fury** up even alone: its threat does nothing solo, but **Improved Righteous Fury** (6% less damage taken) only works while it is on, and the fight lab assumed it always up.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready, with **Swift Judgement** right after a **Judgement** (off the global cooldown, once a minute): it finishes the cooldown and makes the next one free. **Sanctified Judgement** returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time you judge.

**Consecration** only while your mana is above 60%, a hand-set rule the fight lab plays (no search has tuned this rotation yet); **Holy Conduit** makes it and **Hammer of Wrath** 40% cheaper. **Hammer of Wrath** finishes mobs below 20% health from level 44.

Below about a third of your health: **Templar's Bulwark** first (an absorb as large as your health for 8 seconds), then **Holy Light** behind it. The fight lab casts **Holy Light** only while the mob cannot hurt you: inside the absorb, during **Divine Protection** or while **Hammer of Justice** holds it; **Lay on Hands** below 15%.
caveats: **Holy Shield** is not in this build (it needs 30 points in Protection first): skip its line.
**Templar's Bulwark** applies Forbearance for a minute, so **Divine Protection** is not available right after it.
Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** (instant, 15-second cooldown, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**) hits them hard. The fight lab has no such mobs, so it was not measured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.
Two or more mobs: **Consecration** hits them all; the 60% mana rule was set for single mobs, and this rotation was not measured on several.
Tanking a dungeon on the way: **Seal of Fury**'s judgement taunts for 4 seconds, and **Righteous Fury** makes your Holy damage 60% more threat.

raid.plan: You heal with two spells: **Holy Light** on the tank, in the rank that covers what he is missing, and **Flash of Light** on everyone else. **Holy Shock**, **Divine Favor** and **Lay on Hands** are for emergencies, and your critical heals pay part of their mana back.
why: Keep **Blessing of Light** on the tank: it adds up to 400 to each **Holy Light** and 115 to each **Flash of Light** he receives. Start a **Holy Light** when he is missing at least half of one and more hits are coming; in the healer lab the two of them do most of your healing.

Downrank: cast the smallest rank that heals about what the target is missing. Forever gives ranks far below your level less of your +healing (TBC's rule, our assumption): **Holy Light** ranks 7 to 9 and **Flash of Light** ranks 5 and 6 lose nothing or almost nothing, while rank 6 **Holy Light** keeps 85% of the bonus and lower ranks less, so stay near the top.

**Flash of Light** is your raid heal: the lab heals other raid members only once they fall below half health, which measured about 1% more healing capacity than starting at 70%, and it tops up the tank when he misses most of a **Flash of Light**.

**Holy Shock** is instant but small (307 to 333 at rank 4): keep it for anyone under a quarter of their health, where speed matters more than size; the lab measured that threshold better than 35%. **Divine Favor** (2-minute cooldown) goes before a top-rank **Holy Light** on a tank who is missing most of one: a sure critical heal.

Mana: **Illumination** returns half the base cost of each critical **Holy Light**, **Flash of Light**, **Holy Shock** or **Light's Vigil** heal, **Holy Power** adds 5% crit to your heals, and **Reverence** keeps 30% of your mana regeneration going while you cast. Drink a mana potion as soon as you are below 80% mana (after the first 45 seconds); the lab measured that better than waiting for 65%.
**Lay on Hands** is for a tank about to die (the lab uses it under 20% health): it heals him for your maximum health but drains all your mana, and its 20-minute cooldown makes it once a fight.
caveats: The healer lab is this project's model of stated assumptions: one tank under boss melee and four raid members under raid damage for five minutes, with no dispels and no spell pushback. Check its numbers at launch.

**Light's Vigil**, your last talent, is a two-step group heal: put it on a party member, then **Holy Shock** them to heal their whole party for 684 to 724, with no cooldown on that **Holy Shock**. It costs 1,340 mana, so the healer lab casts it only when at least three raid members besides the tank are below half health.

**Infusion of Light**: a critical **Holy Shock** or **Flash of Light** makes your next **Holy Light** within 15 seconds 1 second faster, so follow such a crit with **Holy Light** when the tank needs one.
diverge: When a whole party is taking damage, **Light's Vigil** and **Holy Shock** are your only group heal; otherwise heal the lowest member with **Flash of Light**.
**Cleanse** a harmful magic, poison or disease effect when it would cost more healing than the cast; the lab has no debuffs, so when is your call.

leveling.plan: Holy levels as a two-handed **Seal of Righteousness** paladin who heals itself. The order takes its Retribution points first, so for most levels you judge and **Holy Strike**; **Divine Favor** and **Holy Shock** come only at levels 58 and 59.
why: **Blessing of Wisdom** instead of **Blessing of Might**: the fight lab found the blessings within about 2% of each other for this build, and Wisdom's mana keeps coming while you fight and cast. **Seal of Righteousness** is your only damage seal, since this build has no **Seal of Command**.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready: **Judgement** is off the global cooldown, back every 8 seconds with **Improved Judgement** (levels 15 and 16), and **Sanctified Judgement** (from level 20) returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time.

**Holy Shock** opens at range as the mob walks in, but only while your mana is above about 70%: below that, its mana is worth more as heals. **Holy Power** adds 15% crit to it, and **Divine Favor** makes it a sure critical hit while you are healthy.

Heal in the fight once you drop below 40% health and the mob has more than a fifth left: **Holy Shock** on yourself first (instant), **Divine Protection** below 30%, **Hammer of Justice**, then **Holy Light**. Critical heals return half their base cost through **Illumination**, and **Spiritual Focus** protects 70% of your heals from pushback.

Not on the list: **Consecration** and **Hammer of Wrath**. The fight lab never casts **Consecration** as Holy (its mana buys more as heals and less drinking), and its tuned rotation skips **Hammer of Wrath** for about 1% faster kills; this build has no **Holy Conduit** to make either cheaper.
caveats: Until levels 58 and 59, skip the **Holy Shock** and **Divine Favor** lines: this order takes them last. Before that your in-fight heal is **Holy Light**, safest behind **Divine Protection** or a **Hammer of Justice** stun.

Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** and **Holy Wrath** come back a third faster with **Purifying Power** (levels 41 and 42), so use **Exorcism** on cooldown against them. The fight lab has no such mobs, so this is unmeasured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.

leveling.plan: Prot-Ret plays like Protection (a one-hander, a shield and **Seal of Fury**) but spends its deeper points on Retribution's crit, **Vengeance** and cheaper Holy spells. Blocks and used-up **Seal of Fury** shields pay for **Consecration**.
why: **Seal of Fury** before each pull: 35 Holy damage on every swing at rank 7 and, with a shield, an absorb of half of it. **Improved Seal of Fury** returns 60 mana each time that absorb is used up and **Shield Specialization** 6% of your mana on a block (once every 3 seconds); the open search found **Improved Seal of Fury** worth about 3 seconds per kill at 60.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready, with **Swift Judgement** right after a **Judgement** for a free second one. **Sanctified Judgement** returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time you judge, and **Sacred Arbiter** adds 20% to **Holy Strike**.

**Consecration** while your mana is above 60%: **Holy Conduit** makes it 40% cheaper, and the open search found **Holy Conduit** the most valuable talent of this build at 60 (about 3.3 seconds per kill).
**Hammer of Wrath** finishes mobs below 20% health from level 44; 1 point in **Instrument of Law** cuts its cast by half a second.

Low on health: this build has no **Templar's Bulwark**, so use **Divine Protection** below 30% or a **Hammer of Justice** stun and cast **Holy Light** while the mob cannot hit you; **Flash of Light** below a quarter, **Lay on Hands** below 15%.
caveats: **Holy Shield** and **Templar's Bulwark** are not in this build: skip their lines.

The order spends levels 10 to 31 in Protection, starting with defensive talents (**Redoubt**, **Anticipation**, **Shield Specialization**), so early kills are slow: about 33 seconds at level 20 against 27 at 30.
Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** (40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**) hits them hard; the fight lab has no such mobs, so it was not measured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.
Two or more mobs: **Consecration** hits them all; the 60% mana rule was set for single mobs.
